transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. I work in computer support, and... I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times, and I still don't actually know what they say. It's just getting impossible to get things done.
Has trouble focusing like this been a problem for you since childhood or your school years, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

It's definitely been around since I was a kid. My mother actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says the teachers always wrote that I was a bright kid, but... I just never stayed in my seat. I was always blurting out answers in class, and I'd constantly lose my homework, even when I had actually taken the time to do it. So, yeah, it's not a new thing at all.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm frustrated with my work and how hard it is to just get things done, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I still enjoy the things I usually like to do when I have the time for them. It's really just the focus and the constant distraction that's the problem.
